items.quote: We have built our adviser business around helping independent advisers grow, compete and succeed.

items.text: Schwab says it maintains its competitive position in RIA custody primarily through its sales, support, technology, and business consulting teams dedicated to helping RIAs grow, compete, and succeed.
items.quote: Management believes that we can maintain our competitive position primarily through the efforts of our sales, support, technology, and business consulting teams, which are dedicated to helping RIAs grow, compete, and succeed in serving their clients.

items.text: CEO Rick Wurster said Schwab will continue to focus on its custody services for registered investment advisors with under $100 million AUM.
items.quote: Schwab will continue to focus on its custody services for registered investment advisors with under $100 million AUM, President and CEO Rick Wurster told an audience of advisors at Schwab Impact

items.text: Wurster said Schwab's role is to provide a platform and a support ecosystem that helps RIA firms support their clients and thrive.
items.quote: Our job and our role is to provide a platform and a support ecosystem that helps you support your clients and helps your firm thrive.

items.text: Schwab's stated strategy includes being the leading RIA support ecosystem, providing wealth tools, investment and lending products, and technology in addition to custody and service.
items.quote: The leading RIA support ecosystem to help advisors serve their clients, providing wealth tools, investment / lending products, & technology in addition to custody & service

items.text: Schwab wants to give RIAs equal or better access than their wirehouse counterparts to banking services such as lending, private market investing, and long-short investment strategies.
items.quote: Schwab wants to give registered investment advisors equal or better access than their wirehouse counterparts to banking services such as lending , private market investing, and long-short investment strategies

cells.reason: The passages state Schwab's overall strategy for its RIA custody/adviser business.

cells.label: fact

items.text: Schwab describes its Advisor Services segment as providing custodial, trading, banking and trust, and support services to independent RIAs, independent retirement advisors, and recordkeepers.
items.quote: The Advisor Services segment provides custodial, trading, banking and trust, and support services to independent registered investment advisors (RIAs), independent retirement advisors, and recordkeepers.

items.text: Schwab says it serves more than 16,000 RIA firms representing $5.8 trillion in assets with a platform that brings together custody, trading, banking and lending capabilities, technology, and dedicated service and support.
items.quote: we serve more than 16,000 firms representing $5.8 trillion in assets with a platform that brings together custody, trading, banking and lending capabilities, technology and dedicated service and support.

items.text: Schwab says that as custodian it earns revenue from the underlying client assets, predominantly through net interest revenue and asset management and administration fees, and does not charge the RIA or end client a custody fee.
items.quote: By functioning as the custodian, Schwab earns revenue associated with the underlying client assets, predominantly through net interest revenue and asset management and administration fees. In this capacity, we do not charge the RIA or end client a custody fee.

items.text: Schwab says RIAs who custody client accounts at Schwab may use proprietary software for client account information and trading, with the Advisor Services website as the core platform for daily business activities.
items.quote: RIAs who custody client accounts at Schwab may use proprietary software that provides them with up-to-date client account information as well as trading capabilities. The Advisor Services website is the core platform for RIAs to conduct daily business activities online with Schwab

items.text: Schwab describes Advisor Services as being in a position of strength and a driving force for Schwab, with $5.2 trillion in client assets, 16,000 advisory firms, and 3.9 million households, ranking #1 in RIA custodial assets.
items.quote: Advisor Services is in a position of strength & remains a driving force for Schwab. $5.2T Client Assets 16K Advisory Firms Households 3.9M in RIA Custodial Assets #1

items.text: Schwab describes its offering to independent, fee-based investment advisors as custodial, operational and trading support through Schwab Advisor Services.
items.quote: custodial, operational and trading support for independent, fee-based investment advisors through Schwab Advisor Services TM

cells.reason: The passages describe Schwab's RIA custody business and its offering.

cells.label: fact

items.text: Schwab says its strategic priorities in Advisor Services include expanding its wealth services offer, designed to simplify processes and help advisors compete and serve clients' comprehensive needs.
items.quote: First is wealth. We're expanding our wealth services offer, which is designed to simplify processes and help advisors compete and serve their clients' comprehensive needs.

items.text: Schwab says it is focused on expanding lending and trust services to advisors through Charles Schwab Bank and delivering industry-leading trading capabilities.
items.quote: Second, we're focused on expanding our lending and trust services to our advisors through Charles Schwab Bank. Finally, we're delivering industry-leading trading capabilities.

items.text: Schwab says in advisor services it is deepening relationships with the 16,000 RIA firms it serves by building a broader support ecosystem beyond custody, growing lending support, alternatives capability, and its institutional no-transaction-fee mutual fund platform.
items.quote: In our advisor services business, we're deepening relationships with the 16,000 RIA firms we serve by building a broader support ecosystem that extends beyond custody alone to add value for RIAs. We've grown our lending support, alternatives capability, and expanded our institutional no-transaction fee mutual fund platform

items.text: Schwab says it focuses on superior service and uses technology to provide RIAs with a highly-developed, scalable platform for administering client assets easily and efficiently.
items.quote: In addition to focusing on superior service, we utilize technology to provide RIAs with a highly-developed, scalable platform for administering their clients' assets easily and efficiently.

items.text: Schwab cites pledged-asset lending balances, long-short investment strategies, and making private-market investing more accessible as focus areas for its custody offerings.
items.quote: Wurster cited the growing use of pledged-asset lending balances, the demand for long-short investment strategies, and the need to make private-market investing more accessible to the masses as focus areas for its custody offerings.

items.text: Schwab says in advisor services it is adding support and capabilities for RIAs of all sizes while also helping new advisors transition to independence.
items.quote: In advisor services, we are adding support and capabilities for RIAs of all sizes while also helping new advisors transition to independence.

cells.reason: The passages state Schwab's strategic priorities for its RIA custody/adviser business.

cells.label: fact

items.text: Schwab states that in the Advisor Services arena it competes with institutional custodians, wirehouses, regional and independent broker-dealers, fintech custodians, banks, and trust companies.
items.quote: In the Advisor Services arena, we compete with institutional custodians, wirehouses, regional and independent broker-dealers, fintech custodians, banks, and trust companies.

items.text: CEO Rick Wurster says independent advisors are competing against wirehouses that typically have strong banks attached to their advice.
items.quote: If you put yourself in the shoes of the independent advisor, they're competing against wirehouses that typically have really strong banks attached to their advice

items.text: CEO Rick Wurster says RIAs compete from time to time against the wealth divisions of wirehouses.
items.quote: They do, from time to time, compete against the wealth divisions of wirehouses.

cells.reason: The passages include Schwab's own statements naming competitor categories and wirehouses in the RIA custody arena.

cells.label: fact

items.text: CEO Rick Wurster says Schwab changed the minimums for long/short strategies and throttled growth to some extent.
items.quote: as we look to October, where we have changed the minimums for long/short and throttled growth to some extent, the growth has in no way slowed at all in terms of AS NNA.

items.text: Wurster said Schwab limited long-short offerings to clients with at least $10 million in assets, curtailing their use by many advisors.
items.quote: That led the firm to limit long-short offerings only to clients with at least $10 million in assets , curtailing their use by many advisors.

items.text: Wurster said Schwab reduced the Schwab Advisor Network referral network by raising the bar for participation to only clients with over $5 million and RIAs with at least $500 million in AUM.
items.quote: reducing the Schwab Advisor Network referral network by raising the bar for participation to only clients with over $5 million and RIAs with at least $500 million in AUM .

items.text: Schwab says that during the Ameritrade integration it experienced some expected attrition of client assets from retail accounts and RIAs.
items.quote: we experienced some expected attrition of client assets from retail accounts and RIAs, though such attrition was below our initial estimates

cells.reason: The passages include Schwab statements about throttling long/short, shrinking the SAN referral network, and experiencing RIA asset attrition.
